end.summary:
Distinguished observations, hypotheses, laws and theories using dog and boiling-point examples.
Identified a hypothesis as a testable prediction and a law as a repeated pattern.
Practised the scientific meaning of “theory” versus an everyday guess.
Theories-turn-into-laws misconception remained at the end; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Tara practised sorting observations, hypotheses, laws and theories, including writing a testable statement about salt water’s boiling temperature. They used examples to separate a repeated pattern from a prediction. A mix-up remained: they still described an idea as turning into a law once proven, rather than understanding that laws and theories serve different roles. At home, ask Tara to label one everyday example as observation, hypothesis, law or theory and explain why.
